preamble.title: cardano-foundation/cip113-programmable-tokens
preamble.description: Aiken implementation of CIP-113 programmable tokens

cardano/address/Credential.title: Credential
cardano/address/Credential.description:
A general structure for representing an on-chain `Credential`.

 Credentials are always one of two kinds: a direct public/private key
 pair, or a script (native or Plutus).

cardano/transaction/OutputReference.title: OutputReference
cardano/transaction/OutputReference.description:
An `OutputReference` is a unique reference to an output on-chain. The `output_index`
 corresponds to the position in the output list of the transaction (identified by its id)
 that produced that output

programmable_logic/params/ProtocolParams.title: ProtocolParams
programmable_logic/params/ProtocolParams.description:
Protocol parameters stored on-chain, referenced by every programmable-token
 transaction. **Every field here has a named on-chain reader** — that is the
 rule this record is kept to. A writable field nothing reads is a trap: an
 operator rewrites it, the transaction succeeds, and nothing changes.

 Fields are ordered by read-frequency / hot-path depth. `programmable_logic_global_cred` sits at
 field 0 because `programmable_logic_base` reads it once per programmable
 INPUT — the only per-input read in the protocol — so it pays no `tail_list`
 step at all.

 **Two phases for field order.** BEFORE genesis, order by read frequency
 and nothing else — no datum exists yet, so nothing can be misread, and
 this is the last moment the layout is free. AFTER genesis, a new field is
 APPENDED, never inserted: the accessors below are positional
 `head_list`/`tail_list` chains over raw `unconstr_fields`, so a field added
 at the end costs every deployed reader exactly nothing, while one inserted
 anywhere else silently deepens — or worse, silently re-points — a hot
 accessor.

 What is NOT here, and why:
   * `programmable_logic_base_cred`, `registry_node_cs` and the seizure datum
     bound are compile-time PARAMETERS of the delegates. A frozen value
     never needs to be a datum read — it only needs baking into whatever
     artifact is itself the replaceable unit, and the delegates are exactly
     that. Removing a field is stronger than freezing it, but only over
     that field: no upgrade can edit these in place, while the VALUES stay
     reachable one hop away, through a dispatch-layer swap that installs
     delegates applied with the values of the authority's choosing.
   * the three delegate HASHES are baked into `programmable_logic_global`,
     which is why it never reads this datum. The trust chain is
     PLB -> params -> PLG -> delegate.
   * `transfer_cred` / `third_party_cred` remain because `issuance_logic`
     sits on a DIFFERENT chain: it must locate a delegate's REDEEMER to prove
     that delegate covered a minting policy's registry node (Finding 04
     precise delegation). Reading them at runtime is what stops a delegate
     upgrade stranding issuance.
   * `issuance_logic_cred` is the replaceable half of issuance (#129). The
     per-token `issuance_mint` policy is permanent by construction — its
     hash IS the token's policy id — so every rule that may change lives
     behind this credential instead.

fields.title: programmable_logic_global_cred
fields.description:
Field 0 — credential of the `programmable_logic_global` dispatcher.
 **The hot field**: `programmable_logic_base` reads it on every
 programmable input and requires its withdraw-0. This one field IS the
 upgrade mechanism — rewriting it swaps the entire dispatch layer without
 moving PLB's hash, and therefore without moving a single token address.
 First because it is the only per-input read: its accessor walks nothing.

fields.title: issuance_logic_cred
fields.description:
Field 1 — credential of the `issuance_logic` withdraw-0 validator (issue
 #129). Read ONLY by `issuance_mint`, the permanent per-token policy, to
 learn which script currently carries the protocol's issuance rules and
 to require its withdraw-0. Rewriting this field is how those rules are
 upgraded for EVERY token, including ones already minted — the permanent
 policy's bytes never move, so neither does any policy id. Sits at 1
 because it is read once per `issuance_mint` EXECUTION — the ledger runs
 that policy once per programmable policy minted or burned, so a
 multi-policy transaction repeats the read — which is the second-hottest
 read after PLB's.

fields.title: transfer_cred
fields.description:
Field 2 — credential of the `transfer` withdraw-0 validator. Read ONLY by
 `issuance_logic`, to locate that validator's redeemer and check it names
 the minting policy's own registry node. PLB does not read it.

fields.title: third_party_cred
fields.description:
Field 3 — credential of the `third_party` (seize / clawback / freeze)
 withdraw-0 validator. Read ONLY by `issuance_logic`, same reason as
 `transfer_cred`.

fields.title: upgrade_cred
fields.description:
Field 4 — credential of the upgrade-authority withdraw-0 validator
 (trampoline 2). Read only by `protocol_params` — at genesis for
 well-formedness, and on every spend to decide *who* may rewrite this
 datum. A datum field rather than a script parameter so the authority
 itself can be swapped in place.

fields.title: pending_upgrade_cred
fields.description:
Field 5 — the INCOMING upgrade authority while a handover is in flight,
 `None` at rest. Read by `protocol_params` on both the mint and spend
 paths; at genesis the field must be `None`, so a protocol cannot be
 born mid-handover.

 Rewriting `upgrade_cred` in one step is forbidden: a hash for a script
 that was never deployed, or a typo, hands the protocol to nobody and
 there is no repair path, because the credential named here is the only
 one that can authorise the next spend. So a handover is two phases —
 the sitting authority NOMINATES here, and the nominee ACTIVATES itself
 by presenting its own withdraw-0, which is what proves it exists, runs
 and consents. Until then the sitting authority can clear this field.

 Deliberately not a co-signature rule (issue #125) requiring the
 incoming credential's withdraw-0 in the same transaction as the
 nomination — that would silently restrict who may become the upgrade
 authority to parties that can be scheduled into someone else's
 transaction, excluding a governance action, or any authority that
 assembles its approval over days. Two phases demand the same evidence
 without the coordination.

registry_node/RegistryNode.title: RegistryNode
registry_node/RegistryNode.description:
Registry node in the linked list of registered programmable token policies
 This represents an entry in the CIP-113 registry.

 Field order is load-bearing: it determines the CBOR layout consumed by both
 on-chain and off-chain code. The four script-credential fields are ordered
 by the natural lifecycle of a programmable token — `minting_logic_script`
 (mint), `transfer_logic_script` (transfer), `third_party_logic_script`
 (third-party), `unfracking_logic_script` (unfracking) — with
 `minting_logic_script` first because registration is the earliest event in a
 token's lifetime.

fields.title: key
fields.description: The key (currency symbol) of the programmable token policy

fields.title: next
fields.description: The next key in lexicographical order (for linked list traversal)

fields.title: minting_logic_script
fields.description:
The minting logic script credential. The token module's withdraw-0 minting
 logic finds its own registry node by equality on this field — that gives
 it the `key` (the policy id) without recomputing the issuance hash.
 The `registry` validator's mint handler also cryptographically binds
 this field to the policy id
 via `expect_programmable_token_id_valid`, so the field cannot lie.

fields.title: transfer_logic_script
fields.description: The transfer logic script credential that validates token transfers

fields.title: third_party_logic_script
fields.description: The third party transfer logic script credential that handles third-party actions (seizure, etc.)

fields.title: unfracking_logic_script
fields.description:
Credential whose withdraw-0 must be invoked by any unfracking action
 touching this policy — the issuer-declared unfracking constraint
 hook. `empty_vkey` means unfracking is FORBIDDEN for this policy
 (least permission by default: no script, no party). A `Script`
 credential delegates to the issuer's hook validator; a
 `VerificationKey` credential gives signature-gated unfracking (a
 withdrawal against a vkey reward account requires that key's
 signature). Sits at index 5, keeping the four logic-credential
 fields contiguous (2-5) ahead of the scalar `global_state_cs`.
 Freely mutable through the registry-node update path, like the
 other logic fields.

fields.title: global_state_cs
fields.description: Optional global state NFT currency symbol for this policy

types/BaseSpendRedeemer.title: BaseSpendRedeemer
types/BaseSpendRedeemer.description:
Redeemer of the `programmable_logic_base` spend validator.

 PLB runs once per programmable-token input, so its cost is multiplied by
 every such input in the transaction — which is why it does the smallest
 job in the protocol: locate the params datum, read ONE credential
 (`programmable_logic_global_cred`, field 0), and require that credential's withdraw-0 at the
 witnessed index. No arm, no `when`, no choice of accessor.

 It witnesses WHERE the dispatcher's credential sits in the ledger-ordered
 withdrawal map (Script credentials first, then VerificationKey, bytewise
 within each), so the check is a direct `list.expect_at` — O(`wdrl_idx`) cell
 drops with no comparison on the way — plus one equality, instead of a scan
 that compares at every entry.

 Self-validating: a wrong `wdrl_idx` resolves to some other credential and
 the equality fails, so a dishonest witness can only invalidate its own
 transaction.

fields.title: params_idx
fields.description: Index of the protocol-params NFT UTxO in `reference_inputs`.

fields.title: wdrl_idx
fields.description: Index of `programmable_logic_global_cred`'s entry in the ledger-ordered withdrawal map.

types/IssuanceMintRedeemer.title: IssuanceMintRedeemer
types/IssuanceMintRedeemer.description:
Redeemer of the PERMANENT issuance policy (`issuance_mint`, issue #129):
 nothing but an index hint locating the protocol-params UTxO among the
 reference inputs. Everything that could ever change — registry proofs,
 custody, delegate redeemer shapes — travels in `IssuanceLogicRedeemer`
 instead, so this type can stay frozen for as long as any token exists.

types/MintingRegistryProof.title: MintingRegistryProof
types/MintingRegistryProof.description:
Per-policy registry proof carried in `IssuanceLogicRedeemer`.

 The redeemer is the registry proof itself — a `RefInput` index for a
 subsequent mint (registry node already exists), or an `OutputIndex` for
 the first mint (registry node being created in the same tx).

 The token module's withdraw-0 invocation (proof of instance) is checked by
 `issuance_mint` directly against its `minting_logic_cred` parameter — no
 separate redeemer field needed. The validator parameter is baked into
 the policy id at compile time and pinned to `registry.minting_logic_script`
 by the cryptographic binding in the registry validator's mint handler, so
 collision-resistance of blake2b_224 forces credential agreement without a
 runtime equality check on the redeemer.

types/ProgrammableLogicGlobalRedeemer.title: ProgrammableLogicGlobalRedeemer
types/ProgrammableLogicGlobalRedeemer.description:
Redeemer of the `programmable_logic_global` dispatcher.

 PLG is reached from PLB (which named it via `programmable_logic_global_cred`) and does exactly one
 thing: prove that the delegate for the chosen ACTION was invoked. The three
 delegate hashes are compile-time parameters of PLG, so it never reads the
 params datum — the trust chain is PLB -> params -> PLG -> delegate, and PLG
 is the link that turns "some dispatcher ran" into "the right delegate ran".

 The arms carry NO payload on purpose. Everything a delegate needs — registry
 proofs, node indices, output offsets — travels in that delegate's OWN
 redeemer, where the delegate itself validates it. Duplicating any of it here
 would create a second, unchecked claim about the same fact, and forcing the
 two to agree would mean PLG decoding the delegate's redeemer — which is
 exactly the work this design exists to avoid.

anyOf.title: TransferAct
anyOf.description: An ordinary transfer: requires the `transfer` validator's withdraw-0.

anyOf.title: ThirdPartyAct
anyOf.description:
A third-party action (seize / clawback / freeze enforcement): requires
 the `third_party` validator's withdraw-0.

anyOf.title: UnfrackingAct
anyOf.description:
Holder-driven same-owner restructuring (Finding 17): requires the
 `unfracking` validator's withdraw-0.

types/ProtocolParamsRedeemer.title: ProtocolParamsRedeemer
types/ProtocolParamsRedeemer.description:
Redeemer of the `protocol_params` SPEND handler — which of the three
 upgrade-path transaction shapes this is.

 The arms carry NO payload, for the same reason
 `ProgrammableLogicGlobalRedeemer`'s do not: every value the branch needs is
 already in the continuing datum, which is validated regardless. A
 credential repeated here would be a second, unchecked claim about the same
 fact, and forcing the two to agree costs a comparison that buys nothing.

 The arms exist to make each transaction DECLARE its intent, so that each
 branch is one closed rule set rather than a disjunction the reader has to
 solve. Note what that buys beyond legibility: because `ProtocolUpgrade`
 freezes the nomination and `NominateAuthority` freezes everything else, a
 nomination can never ride along inside a parameter change. Anyone watching
 the chain sees an authority handover begin as its own transaction.

 Audit-3 finding 02 (issue #124) is about the PLB redeemer carrying action
 variants: PLB stays action-agnostic because its hash is baked into every
 token address, so an action set change there would be a token-address
 migration. `protocol_params` is the upgrade path itself — replacing it is
 a redeploy by definition — so there is no such coupling to protect here.

anyOf.title: ProtocolUpgrade
anyOf.description:
Rewrite mutable protocol wiring. May change `programmable_logic_global_cred`,
 `issuance_logic_cred`, `transfer_cred` and `third_party_cred`; may NOT
 touch `upgrade_cred` or the nomination. Authorised by the sitting
 `upgrade_cred`'s withdraw-0.

anyOf.title: NominateAuthority
anyOf.description:
Phase 1 of a handover: set (or clear) `pending_upgrade_cred` and nothing
 else. `Some(c)` nominates or re-nominates, `None` revokes. Authorised by
 the sitting `upgrade_cred`'s withdraw-0.

anyOf.title: PromoteAuthority
anyOf.description:
Phase 2 of a handover: the standing nominee becomes `upgrade_cred` and
 the nomination clears; nothing else moves. Authorised by the NOMINEE's
 own withdraw-0 — the evidence that it exists, runs and consents.

types/RegistryProof.title: RegistryProof
types/RegistryProof.description: Proof that a token is (or is not) in the registry

anyOf.title: TokenExists
anyOf.description: Token exists in the registry at this reference input index

anyOf.title: TokenDoesNotExist
anyOf.description: Token does not exist (proof via covering node at this index)

types/RegistryRedeemer.title: RegistryRedeemer
types/RegistryRedeemer.description: Redeemer for registry minting policy (linked list operations)

anyOf.title: RegistryInit
anyOf.description: Initialize the registry with the origin node

anyOf.title: RegistryInsert
anyOf.description:
Insert a new programmable token policy into the registry.

 `minting_logic_script` is the credential of the token module's
 withdraw-0 minting logic. The `registry` mint handler enforces that:
   * the new node's datum field `minting_logic_script` equals this
     value (datum-matches-redeemer check, prevents the registrar
     from writing a different credential into the datum than they
     claim in the redeemer);
   * the issuance template parameterised with this credential hashes
     to `key` (cryptographic binding: the `hashed_param` used in the
     policy id derivation is the inner 28-byte hash of this
     credential — derived inside the validator, NOT supplied as a
     separate redeemer field);
   * the token module's withdraw-0 logic is invoked
     (`minting_logic_script` in `tx.withdrawals`).

 Whether the registration also carries a first mint of the new
 policy is NOT constrained by the `registry` mint handler: a first mint in the
 same tx is validated by `issuance_mint` as usual, and registering
 without any mint is equally valid (useful for real-world-asset
 issuance or supply-aware token modules that must initialise global
 state before any token exists). A token module that wants a strict
 register-then-mint lifecycle must enforce it in its own minting
 logic.

types/ThirdPartyRedeemer.title: ThirdPartyRedeemer
types/ThirdPartyRedeemer.description:
Redeemer of the standalone `third_party` withdraw-0 validator.
 Same index-hint discipline as `UnfrackingRedeemer`: a third-party
 (seize / clawback / freeze-enforcement) action names its subject
 policy's registry node and pairs every acted-on PLB input positionally
 with a continuing output starting at `outputs_start_idx`.

fields.title: registry_node_idx
fields.description: Index of the subject policy's registry node in reference inputs

fields.title: outputs_start_idx
fields.description: Starting index in outputs where processed outputs begin

types/TransferRedeemer.title: TransferRedeemer
types/TransferRedeemer.description:
Redeemer of the `transfer` withdraw-0 validator — the script every
 ordinary programmable-token transfer is dispatched to, by
 `programmable_logic_global` under a `TransferAct` arm.

 This redeemer carries no `params_idx`: the `transfer` validator does not
 read the protocol-params datum. `programmable_logic_base_cred`,
 `registry_node_cs` and the seizure datum bound are compile-time parameters
 of the validator instead. Same for the standalone `third_party` and
 `unfracking` redeemers.

fields.title: proofs
fields.description: One registry proof per distinct spent policy, in ascending policy order

types/UnfrackingRedeemer.title: UnfrackingRedeemer
types/UnfrackingRedeemer.description:
Redeemer of the standalone `unfracking` withdraw-0 validator.
 Same index-hint discipline as `ThirdPartyRedeemer`: an unfracking action
 is single-policy, names its registry node, and pairs every PLB input
 positionally with a continuing output starting at `outputs_start_idx`.

fields.title: registry_node_idx
fields.description: Index of the acted-on policy's registry node in reference inputs

fields.title: outputs_start_idx
fields.description: Starting index in outputs where the paired continuing outputs begin
